description:
Goal: Return canonical bottom before constructing a tuple when any already-interned tuple field is the canonical bottom Ty.

Signal: `Types::tuple` always allocates a tuple descriptor and enters `Types::intern`; the existing type tests prove `tuple([int, none]) = none`. Thus a shallow scan over immutable Ty handles can decide that construction before descriptor-level tuple-emptiness normalization traverses the field descriptors.

Strategy: First measure the current interning work for a tuple containing `none`, then add the shallow public-boundary short circuit only if it preserves the exact existing law. Keep descriptor emptiness for arbitrary descriptors that have no Ty and do not add a hash/cache.

TDD and acceptance: Assert semantic bottom plus zero interning work, exercise a nested tuple/enum canary, document the product-factor law, and complete fmt, check, strict Clippy, full tests, cold review, one commit, and close.
title: Return impossible tuple construction before descriptor normalization
